question: The consequences of the lack of comprehensive flood protection planning by the selectively incapable bourgeois state in Crete are enormous. Disastrous floods have put hundreds of people’s lives at risk. There has been incalculable damage to infrastructure, housing, agricultural crops and livestock.

Those affected by the 2022 floods in Agios Vasileios, the 2025 wildfire in Ierapetra and the 2019 flooding in Platanias are still waiting for compensation. Progress on flood defence projects has been sluggish, while in Arkalochori, residents are still living in containers.

The government and local administration are largely responsible, having promoted private and other investments in the interests of capital by means of facilitation and fast-track procedures, while necessary works have been left on the back burner for years. In light of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.

What is its position on the call for the so-called ‘EU Solidarity Fund’ to be used to immediately and fully repair all infrastructure destroyed or damaged by the recent bad weather in Crete, with 100 % compensation for those affected, without any terms and conditions or EUSF limits, with a simultaneous freeze on their debts, and the full restoration of and support for farmers for damage to their crops, as well as for livestock farmers?

What is its position on the immediate, generous funding of all the island’s necessary flood protection projects and infrastructure, which have been in a state of limbo for years, and on the guidelines set out in Directive 2007/60/EC, which weighs up the lives and safety of residents on the basis of the cost-benefit criterion for each project?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.11.2026) 1. The EU Solidarity Fund (EUSF)1 can only be activated at the request of Greece which has a deadline of 12 weeks as from when the first damage occurred, demonstrating that the total direct damage exceeds the thresholds specified in Article 2 Regulation (EC) No 2012/2002.

The EUSF may cover a part of the costs for emergency and recovery operations incurred by public authorities2. Greece’s Common Agricultural Policy Strategic Plan3 allows financial support to farmers and stockbreeders affected by natural disasters.

The aid helps cover eligible repair and recovery costs, including rebuilding farms, restoring buildings, equipment and infrastructure, and replacing affected plants and livestock, so that beneficiaries can continue their agricultural activity locally4. 2. In the programming period 2021-2027, Cohesion Policy supports flood protection actions with EUR 21.9 million in Crete.

The region also receives additional funding from the sectoral programmes ‘Environment and Climate Change’ with EUR 213 million and ‘Civil Protection’ with EUR 133 million. In the programming period 2014-2020, 14 projects worth EUR 8 million were implemented in Crete to address specific risks, ensure disaster resilience and develop disaster management systems.

Directive 2007/60/EC5 establishes a framework for the assessment and management of flood risks, aiming at the reduction of the adverse consequences for human health, the environment, cultural heritage and economic activity associated with floods. The Directive requests Member States to produce Flood Risk Management Plans.
The second Flood Risk Management Plan for Crete6 was finalised in May 2025 which the Commission is assessing. Its revision was co-financed by the EU.
1 Council Regulation (EC) No 2012/2002 of 11 November 2002 establishing the European Union Solidarity

Fund (OJ L 311, 14.11.2002, p. 3) as amended by Regulation (EU) No 661/2014 of the European Parliament and the Council of 15 May 2014 (OJ L 189, 27.6.2014, p. 143) and by Regulation (EU) 2020/461 of the European Parliament and the Council of 30 March 2020 (OJ L 99, 31.3.2020, p. 9). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legalcontent/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:32002R2012.
2 This means, for example, the recovery of essential infrastructure, provision of temporary accommodation to the population, cleaning-up operations, and protection of the cultural heritage.
